was in focus on Friday as Bank of America wondered whether Wall Street's estimates may be “mismodeled” after the tech giant switched up its product release schedule and staggered its iPhone launch.

“As we head into F4Q26 (Sep Q) earnings after market close on Mon., Nov 2nd, investor focus will likely be on component cost inflation, durability of GM and services revenue growth,” Bank of America analyst Wamsi Mohan wrote in a note to clients. “We have incorporated a more conservative outlook overall given the staggered launch of iPhones (Pro, Pro Max and Duo in Sep. and base model, Air in March) and higher prices in response to component cost inflation. In our view, consensus is too high for revs in Dec., GMs in March and too low for revs in the June qtr (but too high for GMs) given the staggered launch this year. We lower our F27 iPhone est. by 9M units to 247M (vs. St. at 260M). Our F4QE rev/EPS are $113bn/$1.97 vs. St. at $114bn/$1.99. Our F1Q27 rev/EPS are meaningfully below St. but could prove conservative esp. on gross margins depending on residual tariff refunds and memory inventory. We view margin pressure as transitory and model higher margins starting end of F27 into F28.”
Mohan has a Buy rating and a $370 price target on Apple.

title: Apple in focus as BofA questions Wall Street estimates amid staggered iPhone launch
